name: Kallazhagar Temple, Alagar Koil
deity: Vishnu as Sundararaja Perumal, worshipped as Kallazhagar, standing, with the Goddess Sundaravalli Thayar
period: A Divya Desam of the Pandya country at the foot of the Alagar hills, sung by several Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
summary: At the foot of the forested Alagar hills, Vishnu stands as Kallazhagar, the beautiful lord of Thirumaliruncholai, who rides down to the Vaigai each Chithirai to a welcome from all of Madurai.

sections.history: Known to the Alvars as Thirumaliruncholai, the 'great dark grove', Alagar Koil lies about twenty kilometres north-east of Madurai where the Alagar hills meet the plain. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams of the Pandya country, and few are so richly sung: Nammalvar gave it three decads of his Tiruvaimozhi, Thirumangai Alvar more than thirty verses, and Periyalvar, Andal, Bhoothathalvar and Peyalvar all praise the hill and its lord. The Pandyas were early patrons, and Jatavarman Sundara Pandya in the thirteenth century is remembered for covering the sanctum tower in gold. The Madurai Nayaks shaped the festival life that defines the temple today: under Thirumalai Nayak, in 1653, part of the Chithirai rites was moved to a mandapam he built at Vandiyur on the Vaigai.
sections.architecture: The walled temple covers about two acres beneath the wooded slope, entered through a five-tiered gopuram. Over the sanctum rises the Somachandra vimana, whose gold covering is credited to the Pandya kings. The halls are rich in Nayak-period carving, above all the kalyana mandapam, whose pillars carry the lively sculpture of that age. Above the temple, a path climbs the hill to the spring of Noopura Gangai, the sacred water of the shrine, said to flow from the anklet of the lord.
sections.legends: The best-loved story is that of the sage Manduka, cursed to live as a frog, whom Azhagar releases by descending from his hill to the banks of the Vaigai — the legend re-enacted each year in the Chithirai festival. Devotees also cherish the bond between this lord and Andal, who longed for Azhagar in her verses; tradition holds that she vowed him a hundred pots of butter and sweet rice, an offering Ramanuja is said to have fulfilled on her behalf centuries later.
sections.festivals: The Chithirai festival (April–May) is among the great sights of Tamil Nadu. Kallazhagar sets out in procession from Alagar Koil, is greeted by Madurai in the Ethir Sevai, and on the full moon steps into the Vaigai on a golden horse before lakhs of devotees, as the city celebrates the Meenakshi wedding. Vaikunta Ekadashi is also kept with devotion.
sections.experience: Come early, when mist still clings to the Alagar hills and monkeys patrol the outer walls. After darshan of the standing lord, many pilgrims climb on to Noopura Gangai for its spring water, passing the Murugan shrine of Pazhamudircholai on the same hill. Visiting in Chithirai is unforgettable but crowded; at other times the temple is calm and green.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; the Chithirai festival and Vaikunta Ekadashi days are extremely crowded. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Alagar Koil is about 20 km north-east of Madurai by road, with frequent buses from the city. Madurai Junction is the nearest major railway station and Madurai Airport the nearest airport.
